jurisdiction.name: Burkina Faso
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Burkina Faso's AI governance rests on explicit AI clauses in its 2021 personal data protection law (Law 001-2021/AN), which requires transparency of AI-based processing, prior authorisation by the data protection commission (CIL) for predictive AI decision-support systems and limits on automated decisions. A national AI roadmap to 2030 was validated in June 2026 under the Ministry of Digital Transition but has not been published. A 2024 law on information systems security, steered by the same ministry, does not address AI, and there is no AI-specific law. The telecoms regulator, the public procurement regulator, the standards agency and the data protection commission have published no AI-specific rules.
lead_institutions: Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CIL)
narrative.review_notes: On 18 October 2026 the National Assembly, the government portal, the data protection commission, the telecoms, procurement and standards bodies, the ICT agency and the regional central bank were checked. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material from the digital transition ministry, the national cybersecurity agency and the official legal portal. The national AI roadmap, the 2022 application decree of the data protection law and the 2024 information systems security law are listed under Leads pending official texts.

instruments.official_title: Loi n°001-2021/AN du 30 mars 2021 portant protection des personnes à l'égard du traitement des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 on the protection of persons with regard to the processing of personal data
instruments.summary: Burkina Faso's general personal data protection law, applying to automated and non-automated processing by public and private controllers established in or operating from the country, with the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) as supervisory authority; it repeals Law 010-2004/AN. It contains explicit AI provisions: art. 15 bars court decisions based on automated profiling and administrative or private decisions based solely on it, art. 19 gives a right to know and contest the reasoning of automated processing and, where processing 'relève de l'intelligence artificielle', requires the criteria and nature of the data to be disclosed at collection, and art. 31 makes decision-support processing relying on AI techniques for predictive purposes subject to prior CIL authorisation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with explicit AI provisions (transparency of AI-based processing, prior authorisation of predictive AI decision-support, limits on automated decisions).
instruments.current_status: In force. Adopted by the National Assembly in public session on 30 March 2021 (date in the title and the National Assembly PDF); promulgated by Décret n°2021-0276/PRES of 20 April 2021 (text of the promulgation decree published by the CIL at https://cil.bf/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Decret-2021-0276-promulguant-la-loi-n°001-2021-du-30-mars-2021-portant-protection-des-personnes-a-legart-du-traitement-des-donnees-a-caratere-personnel.pdf), which orders publication in the Journal officiel du Faso (JO issue reference not located). Implementing rules: Décret n°2022-0514/PRES-TRANS/PM/MJDHRI/MEFP of 18 July 2022 on modalities of application (listed under Leads). Art. 81 gives existing processing one year from entry into force to comply; art. 82 repeals Law 010-2004/AN of 20 April 2004.
instruments.evidence_reference: Re-checked 2026-10-12: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60) of the National Assembly PDF: first attempt connection reset, retries HTTP 200 application/pdf 733,956 bytes (same file as first read); 36-page text re-read with pdftotext: art. 15, art. 19 (AI transparency), art. 31 (prior authorisation of AI predictive decision-support), arts. 81-83 and adoption date 30 March 2021 confirmed. Promulgation decree 2021-0276/PRES of 20 April 2021 read from the scanned PDF on cil.bf (HTTP 200).

organizations.ai_governance_role: Legislature of Burkina Faso (Assemblée nationale; since 2022 the Transitional Legislative Assembly sits in its place); adopted Law 001-2021/AN on personal data protection, which contains explicit AI provisions.

No official full text or Council of Ministers adoption found; ministry website (mtdpce.gov.bf) unreachable (DNS/proxy). Promote once published. 2026-10-18: still no official full text found; ministry website (mtdpce.gov.bf) still does not resolve; government portal, ANPTIC and parliament site searches show no published roadmap or adoption act. Keep as lead.

leads.title: Décret n°2022-0514/PRES-TRANS/PM/MJDHRI/MEFP portant modalités d'application de la loi n°001-2021/AN du 30 mars 2021 portant protection des personnes à l'égard du traitement des données à caractère personnel
leads.english_title: Decree No. 2022-0514 on the modalities of application of Law No. 001-2021/AN on personal data protection
leads.issuing_authority: President of the Transition / Council of Ministers
leads.note: Signed 18 July 2022; 22-page scan without text layer at https://cil.bf/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Decret-Application-CIL-1-1.pdf (HTTP 200). Covers CIL referral procedures, data-subject rights, controller obligations; whether it details the AI-specific prior-authorisation regime (art. 31 of the law) not confirmed (no OCR available). Record as instrument if AI content confirmed. 2026-10-18 (follow-up): the 22-page scanned decree was read with OCR. Article 31 sets the general prior formalities (request for opinion, authorisation, normal declaration) for all processing; no provision names artificial intelligence, algorithms or automated decision-making, so it stays a lead.
